description: Self-policing rules for the SBG repository itself

rules.description: Freeze placeholder comments and scaffold leftovers inside the SBG repo.
rules.what: Catch placeholder comments and scaffold leftovers before they harden into self-hygiene debt.
rules.why: These patterns often indicate unfinished work or copied scaffolding that weakens the credibility of the framework itself.

rules.description: Freeze marker-heavy comments in self-hygiene scans.
rules.what: Catch repeated TODO/FIXME/XXX markers that dilute the signal of real implementation notes.
rules.why: Marker spam accumulates debt quickly when it is allowed to sit in the repository without cleanup.

rules.description: Freeze empty or whitespace-only files in the SBG repo.
rules.what: Require every file to carry meaning instead of acting as an empty placeholder.
rules.why: An empty file is usually a sign that a change was started and abandoned.

rules.description: Freeze long lines in self-hygiene checks.
rules.what: Keep implementation readable by refusing runs of dense code that are difficult to review.
rules.why: Long lines make it harder to reason about the edifice that the framework itself is supposed to enforce.

rules.description: Freeze UI buttons with no explicit action hook in SBG itself.
rules.what: Require every button in the dashboard and supporting UI to expose a concrete action.
rules.why: Buttons without a traceable action are the exact sort of invisible slop the framework should police.

rules.description: Freeze missing bridge links between UI declarations and handlers.
rules.what: Require the self-hygiene dashboard to expose a clear bridge between markup and handlers.
rules.why: The framework should be able to inspect its own UI structure and ensure the bridge remains honest.

rules.description: Freeze oversized files in the SBG repository.
rules.what: Reject files that have grown too large to remain easy to review and maintain.
rules.why: The self-hygiene framework should not allow one file to become an unreviewable monolith.

rules.description: Freeze self-hygiene rules that lack the metadata needed to inspect or explain them.
rules.what: Require the repository's own hygiene manifest to carry the full explanation layers required for human and AI review.
rules.why: The framework should not be allowed to enforce a policy that it cannot explain or trace back to source.

rules.description: Freeze self-hygiene rules that point to source files the dashboard cannot read.
rules.what: Require every source reference inside the self-hygiene manifest to resolve to a readable file.
rules.why: The framework should not be allowed to prescribe a policy that cannot be inspected from the same UI it exposes.

rules.description: Freeze self-hygiene changes that reintroduce machine-specific paths or local endpoints into the framework.
rules.what: Require SBG's own code and config to resolve environment-specific values dynamically rather than baking them into source.
rules.why: The framework should model the portability it is meant to enforce instead of relying on one machine's filesystem layout.

rules.description: Freeze unresolved merge conflict markers inside the SBG repository itself.
rules.what: Require SBG's own files to be free of git conflict markers before any commit lands.
rules.why: A hygiene framework must never ship half-merged files; that would undermine the credibility of the enforcement it provides.

rules.description: Freeze committed credentials inside the SBG repository itself.
rules.what: Require SBG's own source and config to be free of recognizable API keys, tokens, and private key blocks.
rules.why: The framework should hold itself to the same security bar it enforces for the repositories that adopt it.

rules.description: Freeze leftover debugging statements inside the SBG repository itself.
rules.what: Require SBG's own JavaScript and Python to be free of debugger, console, and breakpoint instrumentation.
rules.why: The dashboard and engine should ship clean; leftover debug hooks are exactly the slop the framework is meant to prevent.

rules.description: Freeze trailing whitespace inside the SBG repository itself.
rules.what: Require SBG's own files to be free of stray trailing spaces and tabs.
rules.why: The framework should keep its own diffs clean so its self-hygiene stays credible.

rules.description: Freeze missing final newlines inside the SBG repository itself.
rules.what: Require SBG's own non-empty files to end with a newline.
rules.why: A hygiene framework should model newline-terminated files so its own diffs and tooling stay predictable.

rules.description: Freeze Python files that fail to parse.
rules.what: Reject any .py file that raises a SyntaxError when parsed.
rules.why: A file that does not parse is broken and cannot run; catching it at commit time prevents shipping dead code.

rules.description: Freeze bare 'except:' clauses in Python.
rules.what: Reject except handlers that do not name an exception type.
rules.why: Bare excepts swallow every error including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, hiding real failures.

rules.description: Freeze overly broad exception handlers in Python.
rules.what: Flag 'except Exception' and 'except BaseException' handlers.
rules.why: Catching the broadest exceptions masks bugs and makes failures hard to diagnose; catch specific errors instead.

rules.description: Freeze mutable default arguments in Python functions.
rules.what: Flag function defaults that are a list, dict, or set literal or constructor.
rules.why: Mutable defaults are created once and shared across calls, a classic source of state-leak bugs.

rules.description: Freeze use of eval and exec in Python.
rules.what: Flag calls to eval() or exec().
rules.why: Dynamic execution of strings is a code-injection risk and almost always avoidable.

rules.description: Surface Python functions that take too many parameters.
rules.what: Warn when a function or method exceeds the configured parameter count (self/cls excluded).
rules.why: Long parameter lists signal a function doing too much and are hard to call correctly.

rules.description: Surface overly long Python functions.
rules.what: Warn when a function body exceeds the configured line count.
rules.why: Long functions are harder to test and review; they usually hide several responsibilities.

rules.description: Surface deeply nested Python control flow.
rules.what: Warn when control-flow blocks nest deeper than the configured depth inside a function.
rules.why: Deep nesting increases cyclomatic complexity and makes logic hard to follow; prefer early returns and helpers.
